hero.title: Which legendary couple are we? The quiz in 12 questions
hero.description: Romeo and Juliet, Bonnie and Clyde or Marie and Pierre Curie? You each answer 12 questions about your story. Then the quiz shows you the legendary couple you're most like, with its photo.
hero.subtitle: 12 questions • 3 minutes each • on one phone

section1.title: How the quiz works
section1.p1: This quiz is a game to play as a couple. It finds the famous couple whose story is most like yours. It asks 12 questions about your relationship. For example, it asks how you met and what you do when you're far apart.
section1.p2: Take the question about how you met. If you answer “love at first sight”, the quiz gives points to Romeo and Juliet. If your partner answers “we couldn't stand each other at first”, it gives points to Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy. At the end, the quiz adds up your answers and keeps the couple with the most points.
section1.p3: The first person answers the 12 questions and then passes the phone. The second person answers without seeing what the first one chose. Then the quiz shows you the legendary couple you're most like, with its photo. It also shows the couple each of you would have got alone and the list of questions where you gave different answers.
section1.p4: You can also take the quiz on your own and answer for your couple. But you won't be able to compare your answers. That's a pity, because two people never tell the story of how they met in the same way!

section2.title: The 8 legendary couples in the quiz
section2.intro: The quiz can give 8 results. Four of these couples were real people. The other four come from a play, a novel or a myth. Here's who each one is most like.

section3.title: The story of 4 couples in the quiz
section3.intro: Everybody knows their names but fewer people know their story. Here is the story of 4 couples in the quiz.
section3.sub1Title: Romeo and Juliet, a story of a few days
section3.sub1Text: Shakespeare wrote the play in the 1590s. The story takes place in Verona, in Italy. Romeo and Juliet meet at a ball on a Sunday evening and marry in secret the next day. The whole story lasts less than a week. That's why people mention them when a couple falls in love at first sight.
section3.sub2Title: Odysseus and Penelope, 20 years of waiting
section3.sub2Text: In Homer's “Odyssey”, Odysseus leaves to fight the Trojan War and takes 20 years to come home. Meanwhile, suitors want to marry Penelope. She promises to choose once she has finished weaving a large cloth. Every night, she undoes what she wove during the day! Their story speaks to every couple who has to hold on despite the distance.
section3.sub3Title: Marie and Pierre Curie, a wedding without a white dress
section3.sub3Text: Marie and Pierre Curie got married in July 1895 at the town hall in Sceaux, near Paris. With the money they were given as a present, they bought two bicycles for their honeymoon. Three years later, they discovered polonium and radium together. They received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903.
section3.sub4Title: Juliette Drouet and Victor Hugo, 22,000 letters
section3.sub4Text: Juliette Drouet was an actress when she met Victor Hugo in 1833. She then wrote to him almost every day for 50 years. That makes about 22,000 letters! Hugo was married and their story was no fairy tale. For example, Juliette lived almost shut away for years because he didn't want her to go out without him.

section4.title: What if you don't get the same couple?
section4.p1: It happens a lot. For example, one of you sees your story as Romeo and Juliet's and the other as Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy's. It just means you don't have the same memories of your early days.
section4.p2: Look at the list of questions where your answers are different instead. The question about how you met and the one about the first “I love you” are often the funniest to compare. Ask the other person to tell their version!

section5.title: What you should know about this quiz
section5.p1: This quiz is a game. It plays with the image we have of these couples and it says nothing serious about yours. These couples aren't role models. Romeo and Juliet die at the end of the play. The real Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow were criminals and their gang killed several people. The quiz only keeps what people remember about them, for example love at first sight or closeness.
section5.p2: Your answers aren't saved, they stay on your phone. We only count which result you get, to see which ones come up most. Your name isn't saved either. The photos were created for this page and none of them shows a real person.

seo.faq1Q: Which legendary couples can you get?
seo.faq1A: The quiz can give 8 results: Romeo and Juliet, Odysseus and Penelope, Cleopatra and Mark Antony, Bonnie and Clyde, Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy, Marie and Pierre Curie, Juliette Drouet and Victor Hugo, or Baucis and Philemon.
seo.faq2Q: How is the result worked out?
seo.faq2A: Each answer gives points to one or two couples. For example, if you answer “writing to them every day” to the question about proof of love, Juliette Drouet and Victor Hugo get points. When you take the quiz together, it adds up your answers and the couple with the most points becomes yours.
seo.faq3Q: Which couples in the quiz were real people?
seo.faq3A: Four couples were real: Cleopatra and Mark Antony, Bonnie and Clyde, Marie and Pierre Curie, Juliette Drouet and Victor Hugo. Romeo and Juliet come from a play by Shakespeare. Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy come from Jane Austen's novel “Pride and Prejudice”, published in 1813. Odysseus and Penelope and Baucis and Philemon are couples from mythology.
seo.faq4A: They are an old couple from mythology whose story the poet Ovid tells in the “Metamorphoses”. They are poor but they welcome two travellers into their home, who turn out to be gods. To thank them, the gods grant them a wish. They ask to die at the same moment. When they die, they are turned into two trees growing side by side, an oak and a linden.
seo.faq5Q: Why are Bonnie and Clyde in the quiz?
seo.faq5A: Because people often say “they're like Bonnie and Clyde” about a very close couple. The real Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow robbed banks and shops in the United States in the early 1930s. They were killed by the police in 1934. The quiz only keeps the idea of the inseparable pair.
seo.faq6Q: Can you take the quiz on your own?
seo.faq6A: Yes. Just choose “On my own, for our couple” and answer with your couple in mind. You'll get a result but you won't be able to compare your answers.
